title: Which way is forwards?

data.source: Fluctuation theorems (Crooks 1999; Seifert 2005) for a driven ring in a heat bath. Simulated: 160,000 exits, 400,000 windows and one run of 7 million steps, seeded.

prediction: With a steady drive the R2 cut count is the entropy handed to the bath, in fixed units. The forward direction that R2 assumes is the direction the fluctuation theorem makes likelier, by a factor e to the x per half-turn. Backward half-turns happen and R2 does not record them. The count C is a different thing from entropy.
baseline: The fluctuation theorems of stochastic thermodynamics (Crooks 1999; Seifert 2005), the exact form of the arrow of time in a block universe.
why: All five predictions held. Shared: an arrow counted in loops. Left over on the physics side: the arrow is derived, with its exceptions and their odds. Left over on the CRR side: R2 puts the arrow in by hand (R2 is an ASSUMPTION), and Phoenix states that "positive S is not entropy". Nothing here separates a growing block from a static one (ONTOLOGY).

forks.symmetric two-sided rule (run): forward to backward as e to the x
forks.drive with a potential: entropy per cut varies; not run

weighs: Mathematics of the chosen model; a growing and a static block give the same ensemble.
result: Leaving a point, the ring reached "a half-turn ahead" before "a half-turn behind" 1.653, 2.719, 7.542 and 53.87 times as often at four strengths of push (x of one half, 1, 2 and 4); the fluctuation theorem says 1.649, 2.718, 7.389 and 54.598. The average of e to the minus entropy over fixed windows was 0.9861, and entropy ran backwards in 0.1598 of them. On a long run with 2320 R2 cuts, the entropy handed to the bath per cut was 1.0 where x was 1. A whole backward half-turn hid inside 0.2526 of the occasions (predicted 0.2689). Sampling the same path four times finer multiplied its length by 1.999 and changed the entropy not at all.

framework.name: The block universe with a thermodynamic arrow

precise_core: Relativity and statistical mechanics; the fluctuation theorems are theorems.
proved_by_others: A broad community over many decades.
differing_prediction: The fluctuation theorems forecast how often entropy runs backwards in small systems, against the plain second law. The block READING adds nothing testable to the physics.
tested: Colloidal beads in traps, single molecules pulled apart, small circuits.
engineering: Free-energy estimates in molecular simulation use these theorems; satellite navigation uses relativity.
admits_open_problems: Why the early universe had low entropy (the "past hypothesis") is openly debated and unsolved.
